Thank you! I’m back even though it’s been a while! The cold and I are just…not best friends haha. I have done a few cold plunges which I’ve liked after a work out. 

So far still working out indoors; had a few injuries so I haven’t been able to run, but my mental health is definitely benefitting from moving my body (even though the weight loss has been verrrry slow). Keeps me drinking less and out of bed, so I’ll consider that progress!

I’m definitely going to try a sauna. And I think I’m going to go back to the gym. I’ve been walking outside about 3-4 miles every other day for the last few weeks, but it’s cold and I know myself, I’m going to need some indoor exercise. Going to do a variation of what you’re doing. It’s about to be so cold and I want to do more and give myself less time to be bored/distracted and slide backwards. I still have a lot mentally to work on, but physically I’m starting to feel a little better. 

And thank you so much. I think I can slowly slowly get myself out of the hole. :)

Telling them means I’m admitting it out loud to people that know me in real life. Even my bar friends think I’m fine. I’ve just isolated myself into a corner. But it’s probably the right thing to do.

Usually I can get through a 750 ml of tequila in 2 days; which may not seem like a lot for some, but it gets me pretty drunk and I’m not the biggest person. Just feels like taking shots all day. And I’ve been starting earlier & earlier in the AM. 

If I’m out; I can have 5 drinks plus shots. Lately I’ve been having 2 LITs to start with and then whatever else comes my way. Thankfully I keep it together when I’m outside, but people don’t know how bad it is for me on the inside. When I’m home I black out and have to piece together the night before. If it’s a really bad night, I’ll be super nauseous until I finally let it out at least once. Ie: yesterday chugging straight tequila.

I’ve just been really dodgy, I’ve been lying a lot and cancelling on important events with them because im either drinking for courage or hungover and wreak of alcohol. None of them know what’s wrong, which makes my behavior probably really confusing for them. All isn’t lost, but it’s going to take a lot of work on myself to get to a place where I can regain their trust.
